title: Rast completes the Red Bull Ring double with a fourth straight win
dek: René Rast won Race 2 at the Red Bull Ring for Audi from seventh on the grid, 0.421 seconds ahead of Nico Müller, as pole-sitter Gary Paffett lost ground at his pit stop.

chapters.title: Rast arrives with momentum
text: Saturday's race had gone to Rast, who started ninth and took the flag after Daniel Juncadella was penalised for his restart and Mike Rockenfeller and Nico Müller let the championship contender through on the final lap. Audi filled the podium, Paul di Resta moved back to the top of the standings on 216 points and Rast, on 174, closed to 42 behind with 84 still to win. Paffett, caught up in a first-lap collision, had left with a single point. Sunday brought a damp start to the day, with the manufacturers' title within Mercedes' reach.

chapters.title: Paffett takes pole by 0.028 seconds
text: The track was still wet in places at the start of qualifying, but the racing line was dry and the drivers went out on slicks. Audi looked strongest early on, with four different drivers topping the times and Rast leading at the halfway mark with a 1:23.866. He stayed there until the last minute, when Pascal Wehrlein moved ahead, only for Müller to jump past the Mercedes at once.

Gary Paffett then went more than two tenths quicker with a 1:23.404 for his fifth pole of the season, and Müller's last-gasp lap fell 0.028 seconds short. Di Resta was third and Wehrlein fourth on the grid, with Joel Eriksson the leading BMW in fifth ahead of Timo Glock. Rast, who did not improve on his time in the closing minutes, lined up seventh. Juncadella was eighth, Edoardo Mortara ninth and Philipp Eng tenth.

Lucas Auer, who spent the first half of the session in the garage with mechanics working on his car, could only manage 14th. Sébastien Ogier was again last of the 19 cars, 0.248 seconds behind Loïc Duval in 18th. Paffett's three bonus points for pole also gave Mercedes the manufacturers' title with three races still to run.

chapters.title: Rast jumps to fourth, Müller takes the lead
text: The start was clean, and Paffett defended the lead from Müller with di Resta in third. The big winner was Rast, who made a lightning getaway and was fourth by the first corners, from seventh on the grid. On lap three Müller got a run on Paffett with the help of DRS, passed him and took the lead.

The order at the front then settled, with Paffett trying and failing to find a way back past the Audi. Auer, Rockenfeller and Wittmann were among the early stoppers for their mandatory tyre change, and Wehrlein was the first of the front-runners to come in. Further back Ogier passed Augusto Farfus after a hard fight, and Farfus then parked his BMW beside the track after 15 laps.

chapters.title: A slow stop costs Paffett
text: Rast made his stop in the middle of the race, one lap before di Resta, and the earlier call paid off: on his out-lap he went past di Resta with DRS to lead the cars that had stopped. Paffett came in a lap after di Resta and his stop took about nine seconds, which was too long. By the time he rejoined, Rast was already there and went past him as well.

Di Resta then passed Paffett on cold tyres, only for Paffett to take the place back a few laps later. Rast closed on Müller and passed him at Turn 3 on lap 28 to take the lead, with the Swiss driver offering little resistance. Jamie Green, who had stayed out longest, finally pitted at the end of lap 29 and rejoined tenth.

chapters.title: Rast holds Müller off by 0.421 seconds
text: Müller stayed close behind Rast to the end and looked down the inside at Turns 2 and 4 on the final lap, but the order did not change and Rast crossed the line after 40 laps in 57:45.704, 0.421 seconds ahead. Paffett took the last podium place, 4.700 seconds back, and di Resta, who had stopped attacking him, was fourth, 6.963 seconds behind the winner.

Eriksson was fifth, the best BMW and one of the best drives of his rookie season, with Wehrlein sixth, Glock seventh and Rockenfeller eighth. Juncadella went through the gravel trying to pass Glock and finished 11th, one place ahead of Green, while Ogier needed an extra stop to clear his windscreen and ended the race 17th, one lap down. Farfus and Auer were the retirements.

chapters.title: Three drivers go to Hockenheim for the title
text: Rast had taken his fourth win in a row, his fifth of the season and Audi's 100th in the DTM, and said he could hardly believe the run. Four races earlier he had been nearly 100 points behind di Resta; now the gap was 30. He had won from ninth the day before and from seventh on Sunday, and called the weekend a mega one. He promised Müller a beer for his help, and Müller, who said he saw no reason to make life difficult for a driver using DRS right behind him, praised the Audi crew for building a car good enough for a one-two. Rast said he could not remember winning four races in a row in any category, and certainly not in a series as competitive as the DTM.

Audi motorsport chief Dieter Gass said nobody in the team had thought about a win before the weekend, let alone two. He also said the team had backed Müller after qualifying and tried to get him in front of the Mercedes cars, and that Rast's start and timely pit stop had done the rest.

For Mercedes it was a bittersweet day. Team principal Ulrich Fritz said it was disappointing to start with three cars in the top four and leave with one podium, and that the manufacturers' title, in the brand's last DTM season, did not make up for it. Paffett said the race from pole had not gone as well as he hoped, but that he had cut the gap to the championship leader and was happy with that. He later said Audi's team play on Saturday had been no surprise and that Mercedes should do a better job of preventing it. Di Resta admitted he had not been aggressive enough to keep Rast behind him at Saturday's last restart.

With one round left, di Resta led on 229 points from Paffett on 225, with Rast third on 199, 30 behind di Resta and with 56 still available. The finale was on 13 and 14 October at Hockenheim. Ogier, whose Sunday had been harder than Saturday's, said his race was split in two: he avoided hard fights early on while a smeared windscreen made it dangerous to drive, and was much happier after his stop, when he followed Rockenfeller for some 20 laps.

facts.v: Rast's win was his fifth of the season and fourth in a row, and Audi's 100th victory in the DTM.
